Open Start and type your shop name and your own limits in the yellow cells: target and floor margin, warning days, packaging and picking cost, payout tolerance and the phone numbers for messages.
Fill Channel Fees with the commission, payment and monthly fee rules of every channel you sell on.
Enter Sales by Month for each channel: orders, units, revenue, discounts and shipping charged.
Add the monthly costs of each channel on Channel Profit. Profit, margin and a check against your goal fill in.
Record every payout on Payouts. The expected net, the difference and a check show whether it matches. Open a row on Payout Issues for each short payment.
Review Product Ranking and Product by Channel each month, then decide on the weak lines on Slow Products.
Keep Customers, Customer Orders, New and Repeat and Cohorts up to date to see who comes back.
Enter wholesale accounts and their invoices on Wholesale Accounts and Wholesale Invoices; Order Rhythm shows who should order next.
Log market days on Market Stalls and set goals on Channel Goals. Regional Sales, Listing Performance and Market Notes complete the picture.

Use the 14 calculators for order profit, channel compare, break-even, payout check, fee rule check, ABC class, customer value, cohort retention, account value, tier check, mix shift, stall day, growth and a commission what-if.
Print 10 sheets and 10 letters, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to open WhatsApp with the text ready.
Read Sales Channels Dashboard and Charts every week: profit, payouts, products, customers and wholesale.
Know your profit, your cash in 13 weeks and your sales tax
Profit, cash in 13 weeks, sales tax and break-even in one file
Profit and loss that builds itself
sales, product cost, fees, shipping, ads, refunds, payroll and owner pay of every month come from your own pages, with gross and net margin against your target
payouts, wholesale invoices, supplier payments, tax, bills and payroll land in the week due and warn you before cash runs low
each marketplace, social shop and web shop pays after its own number of days, so you see which week the money really arrives
Sales tax by region and quarter
tax collected for six regions, the amount set aside and a filing calendar with days left, so a payment never surprises the bank
fixed costs over the contribution margin show the sales you need each month and the months you beat it
Sales by channel after fees and shipping
shows the channel that barely pays once fees, carrier cost and product cost are taken off
wholesale invoices with days overdue and the carrier, ad and service bills due, all feeding the forecast
deposits, balances and freight with their due dates, so cash is ready before a supplier is paid
the value of stock against cash each month shows when buying stock ties up too much of the bank
twelve categories with budget, last month and average, and a warning when one goes over
statement lines matched to payouts, expenses and payments, showing short payouts and unknown lines
every document the accountant will ask for, with owner, due date and status

One row for each closed month: sales, costs, gross profit, net profit and margin fill in from the channel, cost of goods, expense, payroll and owner pay pages; you type only ad spend and refunds.
One row for each channel and month: item sales, discounts, shipping charged, fees, carrier cost and product cost; net sales, fee rate and what is left after fees and shipping fill in.
Cost of goods sold by month and category
One row for each product category and month: units sold, product cost and item sales; gross profit, margin and cost per unit fill in.
Expenses: every bill and card payment
One row for each expense with its category, who asked for it and who approved it; the month, a receipt and size check and the phone numbers for messages fill in.
One row for each expense category with its monthly budget and the person who answers for it; this month so far, the last full month, the 12 month average and a budget check fill in from the expenses.
Payroll: pay and employer cost by team member
One row for each team member and month with gross pay, employer cost and the date paid; the total cost and whether it is paid fill in.
Owner pay and draws by month
One row for each month with the amount the owner takes and the date paid; the profit before owner pay, the share taken and the payment status fill in from Profit and Loss.
One row for each month with the money that came in and went out of the bank; money in, money out, net cash and the closing balance fill in, with a warning under the safety level.
Cash forecast for the next 13 weeks
One row for each week ahead: you type other payments; payouts, receipts, supplier payments, tax, bills, payroll and owner pay come from their pages, and weeks under your safety level are flagged.
Receivables: wholesale invoices and how late they are
One row for each wholesale invoice with its due date and the date paid; days overdue, the status and the phone of the account fill in, and open invoices feed the cash forecast.
Payables: carrier, ad platform, packaging and service bills
One row for each bill the shop owes outside purchase orders, with its due date and the date paid; days left and the status fill in, and open bills feed the cash forecast.
Supplier payments due from purchase orders
One row for each deposit, balance and freight and duty payment of a purchase order with its due date and the date paid; days left and the status fill in, and open payments feed the cash forecast.
Payout timing: expected payouts by channel and week
One row for each channel and sales week with the sales you expect, the fee and hold-back rates and the days to payout; the net payout, its date and its week fill in and feed the cash forecast.
One row for each region and quarter with taxable sales, the rate, the tax collected and the amount set aside; the tax at the rate, the difference, the due date and the filing status fill in.
One row for each region and quarter with the due date, the status, who filed and the date paid; the region, quarter, amount and days left fill in from the sales tax page.
Stock value against cash by month
One row for each month with the value of stock and of stock on order; cash, the share of cash tied up in stock and the days of stock fill in.
One row for each closed month with the profit you want; fixed costs, contribution margin, break-even sales and the sales for your goal fill in.
One row for each month with planned sales, planned gross margin and planned costs; the plan profit, actual sales and profit and the variances fill in from Profit and Loss as months close.
Bank reconciliation: statement lines matched to records
One row for each bank statement line with the record it matches and that record amount; the difference and whether it is matched fill in, so short payouts and unknown lines stand out.
One row for each document or task to finish before the year-end, with its owner, start and due date; days left and a status check fill in.

Sales were {col:pnl.sales} and discounts {col:pnl.discounts}, so net sales were {col:pnl.net_sales}. Product cost was {col:pnl.cogs}, which leaves a gross profit of {col:pnl.gross}, a gross margin of {col:pnl.gross_pct}.

Channel fees were {col:pnl.fees}, shipping {col:pnl.shipping}, ads {col:pnl.ads}, refunds {col:pnl.returns}, packaging {col:pnl.packaging}, payroll {col:pnl.payroll}, other costs {col:pnl.other} and owner pay {col:pnl.owner}.
Net profit was {col:pnl.net}, a net margin of {col:pnl.margin}. The profit wanted at the target margin was {col:pnl.target_net}.
Cash flow statement of a month
Cash flow statement of {set:shop}, dated {today}. Month starting {col:cash.month}.
The bank balance at the start was {col:cash.opening}. Money in was {col:cash.money_in}: customer payouts {col:cash.customer_receipts} and wholesale receipts {col:cash.wholesale_receipts}.

Money out was {col:cash.money_out}: suppliers {col:cash.supplier_payments}, carriers {col:cash.carrier_costs}, ads {col:cash.ad_spend_paid}, expenses {col:cash.expenses}, payroll {col:cash.payroll}, owner pay {col:cash.owner_pay} and sales tax {col:cash.sales_tax_paid}.
Net cash was {col:cash.net} and the closing balance {col:cash.closing}. Cash check: {col:cash.state}.
Cash forecast for a week of the 13 weeks
Cash forecast of {set:shop}, dated {today}. Week starting {col:fcast.week}.

We expect payouts of {col:fcast.payouts} and wholesale receipts of {col:fcast.wholesale}. We expect to pay suppliers {col:fcast.supplier}, sales tax {col:fcast.tax}, bills {col:fcast.bills}, payroll {col:fcast.payroll}, owner pay {col:fcast.owner} and other payments {col:fcast.other}.
The balance moves from {col:fcast.opening} to {col:fcast.closing}. Warning: {col:fcast.state}. The safety level is {set:cash_min}.
Sales tax summary of a region and quarter
Sales tax summary of {set:shop}, dated {today}. Filing {col:taxq.filing_id}, quarter starting {col:taxq.quarter_start}.
Taxable sales were {col:taxq.taxable_sales} at a rate of {col:taxq.rate}, which gives {col:taxq.calc_tax}. The tax collected was {col:taxq.tax_collected}, a difference of {col:taxq.difference}.
Amount set aside: {col:taxq.reserved}. Not yet set aside: {col:taxq.gap}. Due date: {col:taxq.due_date}. Filing status: {col:taxq.status}. Rates are demo inputs: check your own rates.
Expense report of {set:shop}, dated {today}. Category: {col:budget.category}. Budget holder: {col:budget.owner}.
Monthly budget {col:budget.monthly_budget}. Spent last full month {col:budget.last_month}, this month so far {col:budget.this_month} and on average {col:budget.avg12} a month.

Budget against actual report of a month
Budget against actual report of {set:shop}, dated {today}. Month starting {col:bfc.month}.

Break-even analysis of {set:shop}, dated {today}. Month starting {col:be.month}.

For the profit wanted of {col:be.profit_goal} the shop needs sales of {col:be.goal_sales}. Check: {col:be.state}.

Open Start and type your shop name, the safety level for your bank balance, the net margin you want and the phone numbers of the owner, the bookkeeper and the team leads.
Enter each channel and month on Sales by Channel and each category and month on Cost of Goods. Profit and Loss then fills in.
Type ad spend and refunds for each month on Profit and Loss and read the net profit and margin.
Enter every expense on Expenses with its category, who asked and who approved. Set a monthly budget for each category on Expense Budget.
Enter payroll on Payroll and the owner pay on Owner Pay. Both flow into Profit and Loss and the cash forecast.
Type the bank movements of each month on Cash Flow and read the closing balance.
Add wholesale invoices on Receivables, bills on Payables and purchase order payments on Supplier Payments, each with a due date and the date paid.
Type the sales you expect per channel and week on Payout Timing, then the other payments you expect on Cash Forecast 13 Weeks. The closing balance and warning fill in.
Enter the tax collected on Sales Tax by Region and the due date and status on Sales Tax Filings. Rates in the demo are examples: check your own rates.
Follow stock against cash on Stock and Cash, and the sales you need on Break-even.
Plan each month on Budget and Forecast and compare it with the actual result.
Match the statement lines on Bank Reconciliation and list the year-end items on Year-End Tasks.
Use the 14 calculators for profit, break-even, cash, runway, sales tax, owner pay, stock purchases, loans and what-if scenarios.
Print 10 sheets and 10 documents, follow 10 checklists and use the message links to send 30 ready texts.
Read the Finance Dashboard and Charts every week.
